- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -0.67+ in 1–2 days) and prices are rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- Model consistently overestimates in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after sentiment spike) — apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 3 forecast days.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative (0.33–0.67) and news volume is low, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch mean reversion.  
- If sentiment shows strong negative change (e.g., -1.00+ in recent days) and model forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.  
- Model often underestimates in low-news periods — if news volume < 2.0 for 3+ days, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for reduced volatility.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and prices are trending upward, model tends to lag — forecast should be 0.5–1.5% above recent 3-day average.
